## Findings

Across all 6 hotrod services over the last 24 hours, only **redis-manual** reported any error-status spans — `frontend`, `customer`, `driver`, `route`, and `mysql` all returned zero error traces.

Looking at a representative trace (`89e52103a97fd980c331260a8a0da4be`), the call chain is:

```
frontend /dispatch
  └─ frontend driver.DriverService/FindNearest   [OK]
       └─ driver driver.DriverService/FindNearest [OK]
            └─ redis-manual FindDriverIDs         [OK]
            └─ redis-manual GetDriver × 12         [10 OK, 2 ERROR]  ← leaf spans
```

The `GetDriver` spans are leaves (nothing references them as a parent). Two of the twelve retries per trace fail with:
```
exception.message: "redis timeout"
exception.type: *errors.errorString
level: error
```

Every ancestor span — `driver.DriverService/FindNearest`, `/dispatch`, `/route`, `SQL SELECT` — shows **no error status**, because the driver service retries the failed Redis calls and a later attempt succeeds, masking the failure at every level above redis-manual. This pattern (same trace shape, same failing operation) repeated identically across all 20 error-containing traces sampled.

**Root cause span:**
- **Service:** `redis-manual`
- **Operation:** `GetDriver`
- **Cause:** intermittent `redis timeout` on individual `GetDriver` calls, silently absorbed by retry logic in the `driver` service so it never surfaces as an error in any parent span.
